correctness.rationale: The repaired proof explicitly handles the missing q=3 branch in the frozen C_2 argument (RESULT.md line 66): at radical 6 the two survivors are x=2,5, both with x≡−1 mod 3, and one prime can itself cover both indices. The published count was correct but the forced-split justification was not. For either prime equal to 3 its common fiber is forced, and all residues of the other prime work; otherwise the two split assignments are distinct. Radical lifting is exact. Pairwise square differences 3,5,8 force the length-three cases, including the q=5 cases addressed explicitly in the repair. The unique third-index survivor extends to five exactly when 3 divides a two-prime radical; 36−9=27 and the congruence modulo 3 prevent extension to six. This proves all counts, uniqueness when claimed, and the nested-set difference formula. Fresh direct gcd enumeration passed on 550 moduli, including C_2(6) classes [2,5] and C_3(10) class [1]. The corrected full RESULT.md at /workspace/repairs/3/RESULT.md preserves the theorem and scope.
residual_risks: The replay is bounded; all larger primes and lengths are covered by the fiber argument, not by tests. No claim is made about a different initial index or three-prime radicals.

value.rationale: Two prime factors give the first interacting local-fiber case of the established polynomial Jacobsthal invariant. The result completely classifies that natural infinite family, including the exceptional prime-dependent transition from three to five and exact survivor frequencies and prime-power lifts. These are usable benchmarks for comparing more general local covering results, not a cutoff selected after computation.
residual_risks: Value is limited to the initial-square model and at most two distinct prime factors; no general asymptotic improvement is claimed.
